verdicts.flaw_description: "The counts cover the sessions that reached the new page, and a quarter of each segment dropped out before checkout." The post-change counts are restricted to the surviving subset of sessions that got as far as the new page, while the comparison figure is 'the same segment a month earlier' (the whole segment). A quarter of sessions are dropped from the measured population on a non-random basis, so the 4-7 percent lift compares two differently-composed populations rather than isolating the page's effect.

"The figures cover the runs with the upgraded filter in service, and a quarter of each stack's runs were made with the filter bypassed." The reported particulate figures are a per-protocol subset: a quarter of runs are excluded, and bypassing is not random (it plausibly tracks the dirtiest or most upset runs), while the earlier-quarter baseline covers all runs. The 8-14 percent reduction can therefore be produced by which runs were kept rather than by the filter upgrade.

"Pollen counts in each group's district ran a fifth below the previous quarter, and every group lived and slept on the district's outside air." A known asthma trigger fell 20 percent over exactly the comparison window, and the report explicitly confirms the patients were exposed to that outside air rather than shielded from it. Fewer attacks are fully explained by the lower pollen load, so the inhaler is not isolated as the cause.

"Averages cover the patients who kept up the home exercises, and a quarter of each intake let the home exercises lapse." The abduction averages are computed only on adherent patients while a quarter of each intake is silently dropped, and adherence is self-selecting (motivated, less-impaired patients keep up exercises). The 9-16 degree gain over the same ward a quarter earlier is confounded by that selection, not attributable to the protocol.

"Rates cover the trays sown from seed that took a full coat, and about a fifth of each lot's trays were sown from partly coated seed." Germination is scored only on trays whose seed took a full coat, dropping roughly 20 percent of trays; seed that accepts a full coat may differ in quality from seed that only partly coats, and the previous-spring baseline was not filtered the same way. The 6-11 point gain can come from the filtering rather than from the coating.

"Rates cover the boards soldered on the new profile throughout, and about a tenth of each run's boards took one pass on the old profile." The defect rate is computed on a per-protocol subset that excludes roughly a tenth of boards, and boards that took an old-profile pass are plausibly the ones needing rework (i.e. the defect-prone ones), while the month-earlier baseline covers the whole run. The 4-7 percent improvement is not a like-for-like comparison.
